maxExplanation.interpretation: With alpha=0.03, a 6.5304 absolute move implies an update target roughly 217.68 points away from the then-current Q if it happened in one update. This scale cannot be explained by the bounded intermediate reward alone; it requires terminal reward (+/-100 plus territory final), bootstrapping from future Q values, repeated updates, or a combination. Exact update count and per-key reward decomposition were not logged.

behaviorReview.knownStateNoKnownAction: Q5 evaluates every legal action with qTable[key] ?? 0. If no legal action has a known key, all actions tie at 0 and selection is random among all legal actions using the seeded RNG.
behaviorReview.tieBreaks: When several actions share the same max Q value, chooseLearningActionQ4 chooses randomly among tied best actions with the seeded RNG.
behaviorReview.newStateEpsilonZero: With epsilon=0 in evaluation, a completely new state still uses greedy selection over default value 0, so every legal action ties and behavior becomes seeded-random for that decision.
behaviorReview.coverageRisk: Yes. Any state with no known positive action, or only unknown actions, can retain random behavior during evaluation. Unknown actions with default 0 can also beat known inherited negative actions.

limitations.exactUpdatesPerPair: Not reconstructable from current artifacts; training metadata logs game-level hits/misses and table sizes, not state-action update events.
limitations.updateRivalColor: Not reconstructable per pair; original heuristic dataset rival/color frequencies are available, but training update rival/color by key was not logged.
limitations.finalVsIntermediate: Not logged per state-action. Large changes can be interpreted from magnitude and Q-learning formula, but not attributed exactly.
